answer: In an agent economy monitoring a lagoon, agents reporting water levels at a ledge or a nearby knoll must lock $100 in a contract to receive one paid task per hour. Creating more identities yields no free capacity: each additional task slot requires another $100 locked for 30 days. An attacker seeking 1,000 slots must immobilize $100,000, bearing its financing cost throughout the lockup. The scarce resource is bonded capital, so splitting it among aliases adds no advantage.
